WR LVN_ALF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Domain 1: Regulatory & Care Setting Orientation

Knowledge: Understands that LVN scope of practice is governed by the state Board of Nursing via the Nurse Practice Act, and that ALF licensure and staffing requirements are governed by a separate state agency (typically Department of Health, Department of Social Services, or Agency for Health Care Administration)

Knowledge: Identifies the distinction between ALF state regulatory frameworks and federal CMS Conditions of Participation (SNF-focused), and recognizes the federally-flagged elements that do apply (HIPAA, OSHA, federal elder abuse reporting, FDA medication labeling)

Knowledge: Describes how ALF licensure categories (e.g., residential care, memory care endorsement, enhanced assisted living) modify permissible LVN activities, staffing requirements, and supervision structures
Skill: Applies facility-specific policies and procedures that simultaneously comply with the state NPA and the state ALF licensing rules
Ability: Differentiates between tasks within vs. outside LVN scope in the ALF setting and escalates to the RN, Director of Nursing, or provider when a requested task falls outside scope
Domain 2: Resident Rights, Autonomy, and Consent in the ALF Model

Knowledge: Articulates resident rights specific to the ALF model, including self-determination, informed refusal of care, privacy, dignity, grievance processes, and the right to manage personal finances
Knowledge: Understands decisional capacity frameworks as they apply in ALFs, including the LVN's limited role in capacity determination and the obligations for surrogate decision-maker engagement
Skill: Incorporates resident preferences into medication administration, treatment delivery, and care routines without compromising clinical safety

Skill: Documents and escalates potential resident rights violations, including suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation, or involuntary discharge concerns, through facility and state-mandated reporting channels
Ability: Balances safety obligations with resident autonomy, recognizing when a resident's choice creates clinical risk and initiating interdisciplinary discussion rather than unilateral override
Domain 3: Delegation and Supervision of Unlicensed Assistive Personnel

Knowledge: Applies the NCSBN Five Rights of Delegation (right task, right circumstance, right person, right direction/communication, right supervision/evaluation) as the framework for all LVN-to-UAP delegation decisions

Knowledge: Identifies state-specific rules on whether LVNs may delegate or only supervise UAP, and the types of tasks (e.g., medication assistance, blood glucose monitoring, ADL support) permissible for delegation in the state of practice
Skill: Validates UAP competency prior to delegation, communicates task parameters clearly, and performs ongoing supervision and evaluation of delegated care
Skill: Documents delegation decisions, UAP reports, and supervisory observations consistent with facility policy and the state NPA

Ability: Recognizes delegation errors in real time - including task-to-skill mismatch, patient instability that invalidates delegation, or UAP hesitation - and intervenes by re-assuming the task or re-directing care
Domain 4: Medication Administration and Management

Knowledge: Describes the distinction between medication administration (within LVN scope where state permits), medication management (ordering, reconciliation, review), and medication assistance (UAP role with resident self-administration)

Knowledge: Identifies high-risk medication categories common in the ALF population - anticoagulants, antipsychotics, opioids, insulin, and antihypertensives - and the specific monitoring, documentation, and side-effect recognition required for each

Skill: Performs medication administration and reconciliation in accordance with the Six Rights, facility policy, and state LVN scope, including processing new provider orders and managing narcotic inventory and diversion monitoring
Skill: Provides structured oversight of medication-assisting UAP or med aides, including audit of MAR completeness, observation of technique, and investigation of administration errors
Ability: Identifies adverse drug events, polypharmacy risks, and off-label antipsychotic use patterns, and escalates through the appropriate channel (pharmacist, provider, Director of Nursing)
Domain 5: Dementia Care and Behavioral Symptom Management

Knowledge: Describes the stages and behavioral manifestations of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) and differentiates baseline dementia behavior from acute changes suggesting delirium or medical decompensation
Knowledge: Identifies evidence-based triggers for behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) and understands the rationale for non-pharmacologic first-line interventions
Skill: Applies person-centered communication strategies and leads UAP in the consistent use of non-pharmacologic behavioral interventions
Skill: Monitors residents receiving antipsychotic medications for appropriate indication, informed consent, efficacy, and adverse effects, and communicates findings to the prescriber

Ability: Recognizes when behavioral escalation exceeds the facility's care capacity and initiates the appropriate clinical response, up to and including provider consultation or transfer to a higher level of care
Domain 6: Change in Condition Assessment and Escalation

Knowledge: Identifies signs of acute change in condition that require urgent escalation - altered mental status, respiratory distress, suspected cardiovascular or neurologic event, sepsis indicators, uncontrolled pain, or functional decline
Knowledge: Describes structured communication frameworks used in the ALF setting, including SBAR and INTERACT tools (Stop and Watch, Change in Condition, Care Paths, Acute Care Transfer)
Skill: Performs a focused nursing assessment within LVN scope, synthesizes UAP observations, and formulates a clear clinical communication to the RN, provider, or emergency services
Skill: Documents change-in-condition events, assessments, interventions, and communications accurately and in real time to support continuity of care and regulatory review
Ability: Discriminates between conditions manageable at the ALF level and those requiring hospital transfer, and advocates for the resident's goals of care when transfer decisions arise
Domain 7: Skilled Nursing Tasks within LVN Scope

Knowledge: Identifies the skilled tasks permissible under state LVN scope in the ALF setting - typically including wound care, catheter care, blood glucose monitoring, insulin and other subcutaneous injections, ostomy care, and specimen collection
Knowledge: Understands the additional certifications or standardized procedures required in some states for IV therapy, central line care, or anticoagulation monitoring (INR checks)
Skill: Performs skilled tasks in accordance with current evidence-based practice, facility protocol, and documented competency
Ability: Recognizes when a clinical situation exceeds LVN scope and requires RN, APRN, or physician involvement, and effects the transition without compromising resident safety
Domain 8: Falls, Skin Integrity, and Preventive Surveillance

Knowledge: Identifies ALF-specific fall and pressure injury risk factors, including the comparative lack of clinical supervision, greater resident mobility, polypharmacy contributions, and cognitive impairment
Knowledge: Describes the Braden Scale, Morse Fall Scale, and comparable risk assessment frameworks commonly used in the ALF setting, including the LVN's role within each
Skill: Leads post-fall and wound assessments, implements individualized interventions consistent with the care plan, and directs UAP on turning, offloading, and moisture management

Ability: Integrates surveillance findings across the resident population to identify trends (e.g., recurring falls after medication changes) and communicates these to the Director of Nursing or QAPI committee
Domain 9: Documentation, Care Planning, and Interdisciplinary Communication

Knowledge: Describes the LVN's state-defined role in the nursing process in the ALF setting - typically data collection and contribution to the care plan rather than independent nursing diagnosis or care plan authorship

Knowledge: Identifies the core documentation obligations in an ALF - MAR, treatment records, progress notes, change-in-condition notes, incident reports, and communication logs - and understands how each supports regulatory defensibility
Skill: Produces objective, timely, and legally defensible documentation that reflects nursing process steps within LVN scope

Skill: Communicates clinical information across disciplines and audiences - UAP, RN, provider, family, hospice, pharmacy, and transferring facilities - adapting register to the audience without loss of clinical accuracy
Ability: Recognizes documentation gaps and systems-level communication failures, and raises them for resolution rather than accommodating workarounds that erode regulatory posture
Domain 10: End-of-Life and Comfort Care in the ALF Setting
Knowledge: Describes the LVN's role in supporting residents receiving hospice or palliative care within the ALF, including coordination with the hospice agency as the primary clinical authority

Knowledge: Identifies physical signs of active dying and understands how goals of care shift clinical decision-making toward comfort, including the documentation and verification of advance directives, POLST/MOLST, and code status
Skill: Delivers comfort-focused nursing care - pain and symptom assessment, positioning, oral care, bowel and bladder management - and directs UAP consistently within the resident's plan
Skill: Communicates with empathy and appropriate clinical framing with family members during the dying process and after death, including post-mortem care and notification workflows
Ability: Manages own emotional responses to resident death and models healthy coping for UAP and less-experienced staff, accessing facility and community grief-support resources as needed

WR LVN_SNF.Training Topic / Competency Item: Domain 1: Federal Regulatory Framework and SNF Compliance

Knowledge: Describes the federal CMS Conditions of Participation for Long-Term Care Facilities (42 CFR 483) as the governing regulatory framework for SNFs, distinguishing federal requirements from state-only regulations that apply in non-certified settings

Knowledge: Identifies the mandatory RN on-site 24/7 requirement and understands how this federal supervision structure defines the LVN's practice model in SNFs, including when rural waivers or hardship exemptions may apply
Knowledge: Understands the dual-layer regulatory model in SNFs: state Board of Nursing governs LVN scope of practice, while CMS governs facility operations, care processes, and quality standards
Skill: Applies facility policies and procedures that simultaneously comply with state Nurse Practice Act requirements, federal CoPs, and facility-specific care protocols
Ability: Recognizes when a requested task falls outside LVN scope under either state or federal requirements and escalates appropriately to the supervising RN or Director of Nursing
Domain 2: Resident Assessment and the MDS/RAI Process

Knowledge: Describes the Resident Assessment Instrument (RAI) process, including the Minimum Data Set (MDS) assessment, Care Area Assessment (CAA), and interdisciplinary care planning requirements mandated by federal regulations

Knowledge: Identifies the LVN's permitted role in MDS completion: may complete quarterly (focused) MDS assessments independently and contribute data to comprehensive assessments, but may not sign comprehensive MDS assessments (RN or physician signature required)

Skill: Accurately codes MDS sections within LVN scope, documenting resident functional status, cognitive patterns, mood, behavior, bowel and bladder function, skin condition, and other observable clinical data
Skill: Contributes meaningful clinical observations to the interdisciplinary team during care plan meetings and communicates assessment findings that trigger care area assessments (CAAs)
Ability: Recognizes clinically significant changes in resident condition that require triggering a significant change MDS assessment and notifies the RN or MDS coordinator within required timeframes
Domain 3: Nursing Practice Under RN Supervision

Knowledge: Understands the federal requirement for RN supervision of LVN practice in SNFs and differentiates this continuous RN oversight model from the more autonomous LPN role in non-certified settings

Knowledge: Identifies tasks that require RN presence, RN delegation, or RN co-signature under facility policy and state scope of practice rules, including IV medication administration, blood transfusions, and initial nursing assessments
Skill: Communicates clinical concerns, resident status changes, and care plan deviations to the supervising RN using structured communication tools (SBAR, situation reports, shift reports)
Skill: Accepts delegated tasks from the RN within LVN scope, confirms understanding of parameters and expected outcomes, and provides feedback on task completion and resident response
Ability: Maintains professional accountability for LVN-scope tasks while recognizing the RN retains ultimate accountability for resident care outcomes under the federal supervision model
Domain 4: Medication Administration and Management in SNFs

Knowledge: Describes the medication management system in SNFs, including physician ordering, pharmacy dispensing, nursing administration, and documentation requirements under federal and state regulations

Knowledge: Identifies high-alert medications common in the SNF population - anticoagulants, insulin, opioids, psychotropics, antibiotics - and the specific monitoring, adverse effect recognition, and documentation required for each category

Skill: Administers medications via all routes within LVN scope (oral, topical, subcutaneous, intramuscular, rectal, ophthalmic, otic, inhaled) and recognizes when routes exceed scope (e.g., IV push in many states)

Skill: Documents medication administration accurately and timely in the Medication Administration Record (MAR), including administration, refusals, hold parameters, PRN effectiveness, and adverse reactions

Ability: Identifies medication errors, near-misses, and adverse drug events; follows facility error reporting and disclosure protocols; and participates in root cause analysis and quality improvement activities
Domain 5: Care Planning and Interdisciplinary Team Participation

Knowledge: Describes the federally-required interdisciplinary care planning process in SNFs, including the composition of the IDT, required care plan conferences, and timelines for plan development and revision
Knowledge: Understands the LPN's role in care plan execution: implements RN-developed care plans, documents resident response to interventions, and contributes observations that inform plan revisions
Skill: Participates effectively in IDT care plan meetings by presenting objective clinical observations, resident and family input, and barriers to care plan implementation
Skill: Translates care plan goals and interventions into shift-level nursing tasks, communicates care plan elements to CNAs, and monitors for consistent implementation across shifts
Ability: Recognizes when a care plan is not achieving intended outcomes and initiates discussion with the RN or IDT to revise approaches based on resident response
Domain 6: Post-Acute and Rehabilitation Care Coordination

Knowledge: Identifies the characteristics of Medicare Part A skilled nursing care, including qualifying hospital stays, skilled service requirements, and the prospective payment system (PPS) that drives short-stay SNF reimbursement

Knowledge: Describes the LPN's role in supporting rehabilitation goals for post-acute patients, including coordination with physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech-language pathology services
Skill: Documents skilled nursing observations and interventions that support Medicare coverage criteria, including changes in condition, response to therapy, and progress toward discharge goals
Skill: Communicates with therapy staff regarding resident tolerance, functional status changes, and care plan modifications needed to support safe therapy participation

Ability: Recognizes when a short-stay resident's condition changes in ways that affect discharge planning (e.g., new pressure injury, hospital readmission risk, loss of caregiver) and escalates to the IDT and social services
Domain 7: Delegation and Supervision of Certified Nurse Aides
Knowledge: Applies federal OBRA requirements for CNA training and competency evaluation and understands the LVN's role in validating CNA competence prior to delegation

Knowledge: Identifies tasks that may be delegated to CNAs under state regulations and facility policy, and those that must be retained by licensed staff (e.g., sterile procedures, assessment, medication administration)
Skill: Delegates resident care tasks to CNAs using the Five Rights of Delegation framework, provides clear direction and parameters, and monitors task completion and resident outcomes
Skill: Provides supervision and mentoring to CNAs, including skill validation, performance feedback, and correction of care delivery errors or safety violations
Ability: Recognizes unsafe CNA practice or competency gaps and takes appropriate action, including re-education, re-delegation of tasks, or escalation to the Director of Nursing and administrator
Domain 8: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI)
Knowledge: Describes the federally-required QAPI program in SNFs, including systematic data collection, performance measure tracking, and continuous improvement activities
Knowledge: Identifies key SNF quality measures that LPN practice directly impacts: falls, pressure injuries, catheter-associated UTIs, antipsychotic use, pain management, and re-hospitalization rates
Skill: Participates in facility QAPI activities by contributing data, identifying care delivery barriers, and implementing evidence-based practice changes within the LVN scope
Skill: Uses clinical data from MDS, incident reports, and quality indicator reports to recognize patterns in resident outcomes and suggest interventions to the QAPI committee or RN leadership
Ability: Integrates quality improvement principles into daily practice, viewing adverse events as learning opportunities and contributing to a culture of continuous improvement rather than blame
Domain 9: Infection Prevention and Control

Knowledge: Describes the federally-required infection prevention and control program in SNFs, including the designation of an Infection Preventionist, surveillance protocols, and outbreak response procedures

Knowledge: Identifies common healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) in SNF populations - urinary tract infections, respiratory infections, skin and soft tissue infections, Clostridioides difficile - and evidence-based prevention strategies for each
Skill: Implements standard and transmission-based precautions consistently, including hand hygiene, personal protective equipment (PPE) use, environmental cleaning validation, and isolation protocols
Skill: Recognizes signs and symptoms of infection in residents, initiates facility infection investigation protocols, and communicates findings to the physician and infection preventionist
Ability: Serves as a role model for infection prevention practices, educates CNAs on proper technique, and intervenes when infection control breaches are observed
Domain 10: Documentation and Legal Defensibility

Knowledge: Understands that SNF documentation serves multiple purposes: clinical communication, regulatory compliance, survey readiness, legal defensibility, and Medicare/Medicaid reimbursement support

Knowledge: Identifies the specific documentation requirements for LVNs in SNFs: progress notes, MDS data entry, medication administration records, treatment records, incident reports, and physician communication logs

Skill: Produces objective, timely, and legally defensible nursing documentation that reflects the nursing process (assessment, intervention, evaluation) within LPN scope and supports care plan implementation
Skill: Documents skilled nursing observations and interventions using terminology that aligns with Medicare coverage criteria, MDS section definitions, and care area triggers

Ability: Recognizes documentation that creates legal or regulatory risk (e.g., late entries, alterations, failure to document fall interventions) and follows facility policies for correction and disclosure
